# Palāsajātaka (Ja 307)

**ID:** Ja 307
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Palāsajātaka
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** The Parrot Tree
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/ja307
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul3.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Palāsajātaka* (Ja 307) is one of two Jātakas in the Pali collection bearing this title, the other being Ja 370 [Blum 2013]. According to its commentary, the story was delivered by the Buddha while lying on his deathbed to comfort the Elder Ānanda, illustrating how Ānanda had faithfully attended upon him and generated great worldly merit in a previous existence [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1883; Nyanaponika et al. 2003]. In the story of the past, the Bodhisatta was born as a tree-spirit (*rukkhadevatā*) inhabiting a *palāsa* tree (*Butea monosperma* or *Butea frondosa*, commonly termed bastard-teak, dhak, or "Judas tree") [Blum 2013; DeCaroli 1999; Sutherland 1991]. A poor brahmin cleared the area around the tree and made regular devotional offerings to the spirit (*bhūta* / *bhūtāni*) in hopes of securing wealth [DeCaroli 1999; Sutherland 1991]. Moved by his piety, the Bodhisatta appeared, engaged him in dialogue opening with the words *Acetanaṁ brāhmaṇa* ("Why, Brahmin, though..."), and rewarded him by bestowing hidden treasure [SuttaCentral; DeCaroli 1999; Fausböll 1883; Sutherland 1991]. The Buddha concluded the tale by identifying the brahmin as Ānanda and the tree-spirit as himself [DeCaroli 1999; Fausböll 1883].

SuttaCentral notes that this Jātaka is cited in the *Milindapañha* (Mil 5.3.5, *Rukkhaacetanābhāvapañha*), where the question of whether trees possess consciousness is addressed [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus finds internal Pali text reuse in 11 matches across two texts: seven segments aligned with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (longest §3.1–4.4 ↔ §175_2–181) and four matches with the *Milindaṭīkā* (longest §0.4–1.4 ↔ §909–913), which aligns with the *Milindapañha* connection noted by SuttaCentral [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus records no cross-language matches with Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora [DharmaNexus].
